title: Sharded counter: writes spread over N sub-keys, reads add them up
caption: Counting is commutative, so each reaction can go to any sub-counter; the reader fans out once and sums.

steps.text: Each reaction picks r = random(0..3) and runs INCR reacts:s5#r. The suffix changes the hash, so the four sub-keys live on four different shards.
120 000 reactions/s become ~30 000/s per shard, well under one node's ~100k. Need more headroom? Raise N.
The reader issues one MGET of all four sub-keys and adds them. Cache that total for a second and reads stay cheap too.

scenarios.name: Sub-key shard dies
scenarios.summary: Losing one sub-counter's shard costs a quarter of the write capacity and makes the total read low, not an outage of the whole counter.

steps.text: Writers that picked #2 get an error and simply retry with another random suffix.
The reader's MGET returns nothing for #2. Summing the rest under-counts until the replica takes over; show the last cached total instead.

scenarios.name: Alternative: batch in memory
scenarios.summary: Each handler counts locally and flushes one INCRBY per second: only one write per server per second reaches the key, but a crash loses up to a second of counts.
scenarios.caption: Batching trades a little durability and freshness for far fewer writes; it needs no sub-keys at all.

steps.text: Each handler adds reactions to an in-memory counter: no network call per reaction.
Once a second each handler sends INCRBY with its total and resets. 50 handlers = 50 writes/s, whatever the reaction rate.
The reader does a single GET. Counts lag by up to a second, and a handler crash loses its unflushed count.
